about.summary: GPU Accelerated t-SNE for CUDA with Python bindings
GPU Accelerated t-SNE for CUDA with Python bindings

name: tsnecuda
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set version = "4.0.1" %}

package:
  name: tsnecuda
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/CannyLab/tsne-cuda/archive/refs/tags/{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 33edac78b22f1cce749f1a6fb01a5a344fc80f0c6c0433d050ef9ab8d7d99a87

build:
  number: 2
  # only linux for the moment; needs a CUDA compiler
  skip: true  # [not linux or cuda_compiler_version == "None"]
  string: cuda{{ cuda_compiler_version | replace('.', '') }}py{{ CONDA_PY }}h{{ PKG_HASH }}_{{ PKG_BUILDNUM }}

requirements:
  build:
    - {{ stdlib('c') }}
    - {{ compiler('c') }}
    - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - {{ compiler('cuda') }}
    - cmake
    - make
  host:
    - python
    - pip
    - setuptools
    # tsnecuda links no CPU BLAS/LAPACK itself (its only GEMM is GPU cuBLAS);
    # FAISS carries its own BLAS transitively. Floor FAISS at 1.10 (the newest
    # on conda-forge) so we don't regress to the netlib-era 1.9.0.
    - libfaiss >=1.10
    # Steer FAISS to its self-contained openblas variant. The default *mkl
    # variant is broken against current conda-forge MKL (faiss expects
    # libmkl_intel_lp64.so.2, which oneMKL 2026.x no longer ships), and openblas
    # is lighter and portable. tsnecuda itself does not link this.
    - libblas * *openblas
    # The build skips when there's no CUDA compiler (see build.skip above), so
    # these are always present in a real build; the selectors keep the recipe
    # valid for the no-CUDA metadata pass without jinja control flow.
    - cuda-version {{ cuda_compiler_version }}  # [cuda_compiler_version != "None"]
    - libcublas-dev                             # [cuda_compiler_version != "None"]
    - libcufft-dev                              # [cuda_compiler_version != "None"]
    - libcusolver-dev                           # [cuda_compiler_version != "None"]
    - libcusparse-dev                           # [cuda_compiler_version != "None"]
  run:
    - python
    - numpy
    # keep the FAISS BLAS variant consistent (and self-contained) at install time
    - libblas * *openblas

test:
  imports:
    # `import tsnecuda` does not dlopen libtsnecuda (the ctypes load happens when a
    # TSNE object is constructed), so this stays safe on the GPU-less CI runners.
    - tsnecuda

about:
  home: https://github.com/CannyLab/tsne-cuda
  license: BSD-3-Clause
  license_file:
    - LICENSE

  summary: GPU Accelerated t-SNE for CUDA with Python bindings
  dev_url: https://github.com/CannyLab/tsne-cuda

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - h-vetinari
    - DavidMChan
